tutorial.select-label-type-1: In this Street View image, we have drawn an arrow to a drop kerb. Let’s label it. Click the flashing "Drop Kerb" button above.
tutorial.label-attribute-1: Good! Now click the drop kerb beneath the flashing yellow arrow to label it.
tutorial.rate-severity-1: Now rate the drop kerb's quality. This one is wide and has a tactile warning, so click {{rating}}.
tutorial.redo-rate-attribute-1: Uh-oh — this drop kerb is wide and has a tactile warning, so it's high quality. Click {{rating}}.
tutorial.select-label-type-2: Now let's label the painted pedestrian crossing. Click the "Marked Pedestrian Crossing" button.
tutorial.label-attribute-2: Great! Now click beneath the flashing yellow arrow to label the pedestrian crossing.
tutorial.select-label-type-3: Great! Now you’ve found another drop kerb. Let’s label it! Click the “Drop Kerb” button like before.
tutorial.label-attribute-3: Now click the drop kerb beneath the flashing yellow arrow to label it.
tutorial.rate-severity-3: Now rate the quality. This drop kerb is fine except there's no space to turn at the top, so click {{rating}}.
tutorial.redo-rate-attribute-3: Uh-oh — the missing landing space at the top is this drop kerb's only problem. Click {{rating}}.
tutorial.tag-attribute-3: Good! Labels can also carry tags that add detail. Click the {{tag}} tag to record the missing landing space.
tutorial.redo-tag-attribute-3: Only one tag applies here — the drop kerb has a tactile warning and isn't narrow or steep. Add just the {{tag}} tag.
tutorial.select-label-type-4: Notice that there is no drop kerb at the end of this pedestrian crossing. Click the "Missing Drop Kerb" button to label it.
tutorial.label-attribute-4: Now click beneath the flashing yellow arrow to label the missing drop kerb.
tutorial.rate-severity-4: Now rate how severe this problem is. Another drop kerb sits right next to this missing one, so click {{rating}} — and always use your best judgment!
tutorial.redo-rate-attribute-4: Hmm — the drop kerb next door makes this problem less severe. Click {{rating}}.
tutorial.tag-attribute-4: Click the {{tag}} tag to record that nearby drop kerb.
tutorial.redo-tag-attribute-4: Only one tag applies here. Add just the {{tag}} tag.
tutorial.select-label-type-6: There seems to be a painted pedestrian crossing here as well. First, click on the "Marked Pedestrian Crossing" button.
tutorial.label-attribute-6: Let's label it by placing your label near the center of the pedestrian crossing. Click below the flashing arrow to add your label.
tutorial.speed-things-up: To help speed things up, we are labeling these two drop kerbs, this pedestrian crossing, and this pedestrian signal for you. In the future, you should label all of these yourself!
tutorial.select-label-type-7: Notice that the footpath suddenly ends here. Let’s label this. Click the "No Footpath" button to label it.
tutorial.label-attribute-7: Click on the ground where the footpath is missing.
tutorial.tag-attribute-7: Add the {{tag1}} and {{tag2}} tags — the footpath stops here, but the other side of the street has one.
tutorial.redo-tag-attribute-7: Only those two tags apply here. Add just the {{tag1}} and {{tag2}} tags.
tutorial.adjust-heading-angle-4: Awesome! Let’s finish labeling the last drop kerb in the intersection. First, grab and drag the Street View image.
tutorial.select-label-type-8: Good! Now click the "Drop Kerb" button on the menu to label it.
tutorial.label-attribute-8: Click the drop kerb beneath the flashing yellow arrow to label it.
tutorial.rate-severity-8: Rate this drop kerb's quality — it's wide, has a tactile warning, and doesn't point into traffic, so click {{rating}}. You can also write notes in the description box.
tutorial.redo-rate-attribute-8: Uh-oh — this drop kerb is wide, has a tactile warning, and doesn't point into traffic. Click {{rating}}.
tutorial.walk-5-1: Now you can look for more issues at this location. In this case, notice how there is a pedestrian crossing with pedestrian signals but no drop kerbs at either end.
tutorial.walk-5-2: Yes! I see the missing drop kerbs.

common.label-too-far-crosswalk: $t(audit:tutorial.common.label-too-far-start) Try adding your label at the center of the pedestrian crossing. $t(audit:tutorial.common.label-too-far-end)
common.rate-crosswalk-sev-1: Now rate the pedestrian crossing's quality. The surface is smooth and the paint isn't fading, so click {{rating}}.
common.redo-rate-crosswalk-sev-1: Uh-oh — the surface is smooth and the paint isn't fading, so this pedestrian crossing is high quality. Click {{rating}}.

compass.end-neighborhood: You've explored this entire neighbourhood! Finish labeling this intersection, then click here to complete the neighbourhood.

popup.start-body: We have moved you to a street in {{neighborhood}}, {{city}}! You are currently standing at the intersection. Please find and label all the drop kerbs and accessibility problems at this intersection.
popup.label-shortcuts-curb-ramp: You can also press the <kbd>{{key}}</kbd> key for selecting the Drop Kerb label.
popup.label-shortcuts-no-curb-ramp: You can also press the <kbd>{{key}}</kbd> key for selecting the Missing Drop Kerb label.
popup.label-shortcuts-no-sidewalk: You can also press the <kbd>{{key}}</kbd> key for selecting the No Footpath label.
popup.label-shortcuts-crosswalk: You can also press the <kbd>{{key}}</kbd> key for selecting the Marked Pedestrian Crossing label.
popup.label-shortcuts-occlusion: You can also press the <kbd>{{key}}</kbd> key for selecting the Can't See the Footpath label.
